addressed_issues.reason: Only 28 rows (0.27%) with ≥7 empty cells; they are kept with NULLs since any present fields (category, building, created_at) still count toward volume. Those missing ticket_id are rejected by the ticket_id rule.

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.why: 14 rows carry 'n/a'/'null' instead of a ticket id; without an id a ticket cannot be tracked or deduplicated, so these 0.14% of rows are rejected rather than inflating ticket volume.

columns.name: created_at
columns.why: created_at uses 8 formats; unifying them is required for time-to-resolve and SLA compliance. 1863 values prove month-first and none day-first, so the 1234 ambiguous slash dates are read as mdy; 'tbd' and 0000-00-00 (13 rows) become NULL rather than fake dates.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.why: 48.2% of resolved_at is empty because the ticket is still open; these NULLs are kept (not required) so open tickets are not miscounted as resolved. 956 values prove mdy, so 630 ambiguous dates are parsed month-first for accurate mean time to resolve.

columns.name: category
columns.why: 111 raw spellings split each category (e.g. pest control appears as 4 variants totalling ~1056 rows); without merging, ticket volume and cost by category are fragmented. 13 '???/null/unknown' tokens become NULL.

columns.name: priority
columns.why: Priority is split by casing (critical×564 vs CRITICAL×558), halving counts per level in SLA and escalation reporting; 10 '???/null' tokens become NULL.

columns.name: status
columns.why: 20 rows hold '???/null/unknown' as status; as NULL they no longer appear as a fake status bucket in open/resolved and escalation rate counts.

columns.name: building
columns.why: 19 rows use '???' or 'unknown' as a building name; as NULL they stop forming phantom buildings in volume and cost by building.

columns.name: description
columns.why: 8 descriptions are '.' or 'null' placeholders; nulling them keeps free-text analysis of request types honest. Casing is preserved since text is descriptive.

columns.name: submitted_by
columns.why: The same requester appears in casing-only variants (e.g. 328 vs 320 rows), splitting per-requester volume; only casing/whitespace is normalized, identities are not inferred.

columns.name: assigned_to
columns.why: 30.4% of tickets are not yet assigned; the empty values are meaningful (unassigned queue) and are kept as NULL rather than filled, so staff/vendor workload is not distorted.

columns.name: cost
columns.why: 993 costs carry a '$' prefix and would be lost from total repair cost; stripping it parses them (tested: 0.05% invalid). -1/-999 placeholders (2.9%) would drag average cost down and become flagged NULLs; 'n/a'/'tbd' (984) and empties (35%) stay NULL as cost not yet known.

columns.name: sla_hours
columns.why: 999 marks unknown SLA in 7.7% of rows (557+9 with -1); left in, mean SLA target is massively inflated and SLA compliance overstated. 'n/a'/'null' (1046) and empties become NULL; zero (~4.5%) is kept pending human decision.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Flag for now and investigate the source system. A share this large points to a systematic export problem, not random typos, and rejecting would lose a third of resolved tickets.
options: investigate source: columns may be swapped or mislabeled
needs_human.question: 34.7% of tickets (1683 of 4853) have resolved_at before created_at, by 94–424 days, and the share is the same for unambiguous dates, so it is not a day/month mix-up. How should these rows be handled?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Provide the missing format id. Losing 4.5% of creation timestamps biases ticket volume over time and time to resolve.
needs_human.question: The profiler found 8 date formats, but only 7 could be matched to registry ids. In a test, about 4.5% of created_at values still failed to parse and would become NULL (possibly epoch numbers). Which registry format should cover them?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Treat 0 as a sentinel. A 0-hour SLA cannot be met, so it would push SLA compliance down artificially. Kept for now until confirmed.
needs_human.question: sla_hours = 0 appears in about 4.5% of sampled rows. Is 0 a real SLA target (e.g. immediate response) or a placeholder for 'no SLA set'?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Keep 0. Internal fixes at no vendor cost are plausible; confirm with operations.
needs_human.question: cost = 0 appears in about 3.1% of sampled rows. Is it a real zero-cost repair (internal staff) or a placeholder for unknown cost?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Merge as proposed so category-level volume and cost add up. Revisit if the business reports on subcategories.
needs_human.question: Should subcategory and synonym labels be merged into parent categories: Sprinkler/Fire Alarm into fire_safety, Access Control/Badge-Access into security, Vertical Transport into elevator, Exterminator into pest_control, Housekeeping/cleaning into janitorial, water issue into plumbing?

row_checks.why: 34.7% of comparable rows (1683 of 4853, same share for unambiguous dates) resolve before creation, producing negative resolution times; flagging lets mean-time-to-resolve exclude them without discarding a third of the tickets.

addressed_issues.reason: Only 28 rows (0.3%) have 7 or more missing cells. Rows missing ticket_id are rejected by the ticket_id rule. The rest keep their real values with NULLs, because filling them in would mean inventing data.

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.why: 14 rows carry n/a/null instead of a ticket id; without an id a ticket cannot be tracked to resolution or counted reliably in ticket volume, so those rows are rejected.

columns.name: created_at
columns.why: created_at uses 8 formats; 1,863 values prove month-first and none prove day-first, so 1,234 ambiguous slash dates are read mdy. Mis-parsed starts would corrupt mean time to resolve and SLA compliance; tbd, 0000-00-00 and unparseable values (~4.5% in a test, mostly 10-digit epoch numbers) become NULL instead of fake dates.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.why: 48.2% of tickets have no resolved_at because they are still open; these stay NULL and are not treated as errors, so they do not distort mean time to resolve. 956 values prove month-first and none prove day-first, so 630 ambiguous dates are read mdy; ??? and unparseable values become NULL.

columns.name: category
columns.why: 13 variant groups split categories (e.g. 'Fire Safety' 216 vs 'fire safety' 210; Pest/pest control/Exterminator), so ticket volume and cost by category are fragmented; mapping merges them and 13 placeholder values become NULL.

columns.name: priority
columns.why: Priority is split by casing (critical 564 vs CRITICAL 558, high 575 vs High 535); lowercasing merges 5 variant groups so SLA compliance and escalation by priority are counted once. 10 placeholders become NULL.

columns.name: status
columns.why: 20 rows hold ???/null/unknown as status; keeping them as values would create fake status buckets and distort open vs resolved counts and escalation rate.

columns.name: building
columns.why: 19 rows use ???/unknown as building; nulling them prevents a fake 'unknown' building from showing up in ticket volume and cost per building.

columns.name: description
columns.why: 8 descriptions are only '.' or 'null'; nulling them keeps text analysis and request triage from treating placeholders as real issue descriptions.

columns.name: submitted_by
columns.why: 3 casing-only variant groups split the same requester (e.g. 328 vs 320 rows); normalizing casing and whitespace merges them without inferring identities, so per-requester volume is correct.

columns.name: assigned_to
columns.why: 30.4% of tickets (3,122) have no assignee, which likely means not yet assigned; these stay NULL so routing metrics are not filled in with guessed staff or vendors.

columns.name: cost
columns.why: 993 costs have a $ prefix and would be lost as text; 984 n/a/tbd/null and 195 -1/-999 placeholders would drag down total and average repair cost if counted. Test: only 1 in 2,000 values stays unparseable after cleanup. Zero costs (~3%) are kept as real values pending confirmation.

columns.name: sla_hours
columns.why: 999 (557 rows) and -1 (9 rows) mark unknown SLA in 7.9% of rows; left in, they inflate mean SLA targets and overstate SLA compliance. 1,046 n/a/null tokens become NULL.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Flag only for now and re-check after the multi-format parse. The share is too large to be random entry errors, so dropping rows would badly skew mean time to resolve.
options: Flag only and keep both dates
needs_human.question: 35% of comparable tickets show created_at later than resolved_at. Is this a known data entry or export problem (for example swapped columns or a timezone shift), and how should these rows be handled?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Add epoch-seconds parsing. These are probably valid timestamps, and losing them removes about 4.5% of tickets from time-to-resolve metrics.
options: Add an epoch-seconds format and parse them
needs_human.question: About 4.5% of created_at values look like 10-digit Unix epoch seconds, and the profiler has no format id for them, so they will become NULL. Should an epoch format be added to the registry?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Approve the merges. They describe the same type of request, and a full category list would also let free-text entries be mapped.
options: Merge casing only and keep synonyms separate
needs_human.question: Should 'Exterminator' and 'Pest' be merged into pest_control, and 'Plumbing Issue' into plumbing? Are there other synonym groups among the 111 distinct category values (including free-text entries like 'Elevator A-001 stuck...')?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Keep 0 as a real cost unless the business confirms it is a placeholder.
options: Keep 0 as a real zero cost
needs_human.question: About 3% of costs are exactly 0. Does 0 mean no-cost work (for example done in-house) or an unknown cost?

row_checks.why: 35.1% of comparable rows (1,866 of 5,319) show created_at after resolved_at, which would give negative times to resolve and break SLA compliance; flagging keeps them visible without dropping data until the cause (format mix or swapped columns) is confirmed.

addressed_issues.reason: Only 28 rows (0.3%) have 7 or more missing cells. Rows missing ticket_id are rejected by the ticket_id rule. The rest keep their real values with NULLs, because filling them in would mean inventing data.

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.why: 14 rows carry n/a/null instead of a ticket id; without an id a ticket cannot be tracked to resolution or counted reliably in ticket volume, so those rows are rejected.

columns.name: created_at
columns.why: created_at uses 8 formats; 1,863 values prove month-first and none prove day-first, so 1,234 ambiguous slash dates are read mdy. Mis-parsed starts would corrupt mean time to resolve and SLA compliance; tbd, 0000-00-00 and unparseable values (~4.5% in a test, mostly 10-digit epoch numbers) become NULL instead of fake dates.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.why: 48.2% of tickets have no resolved_at because they are still open; these stay NULL and are not treated as errors, so they do not distort mean time to resolve. 956 values prove month-first and none prove day-first, so 630 ambiguous dates are read mdy; ??? and unparseable values become NULL.

columns.name: category
columns.why: 13 variant groups split categories (e.g. 'Fire Safety' 216 vs 'fire safety' 210; Pest/pest control/Exterminator), so ticket volume and cost by category are fragmented; mapping merges them and 13 placeholder values become NULL.

columns.name: priority
columns.why: Priority is split by casing (critical 564 vs CRITICAL 558, high 575 vs High 535); lowercasing merges 5 variant groups so SLA compliance and escalation by priority are counted once. 10 placeholders become NULL.

columns.name: status
columns.why: 20 rows hold ???/null/unknown as status; keeping them as values would create fake status buckets and distort open vs resolved counts and escalation rate.

columns.name: building
columns.why: 19 rows use ???/unknown as building; nulling them prevents a fake 'unknown' building from showing up in ticket volume and cost per building.

columns.name: description
columns.why: 8 descriptions are only '.' or 'null'; nulling them keeps text analysis and request triage from treating placeholders as real issue descriptions.

columns.name: submitted_by
columns.why: 3 casing-only variant groups split the same requester (e.g. 328 vs 320 rows); normalizing casing and whitespace merges them without inferring identities, so per-requester volume is correct.

columns.name: assigned_to
columns.why: 30.4% of tickets (3,122) have no assignee, which likely means not yet assigned; these stay NULL so routing metrics are not filled in with guessed staff or vendors.

columns.name: cost
columns.why: 993 costs have a $ prefix and would be lost as text; 984 n/a/tbd/null and 195 -1/-999 placeholders would drag down total and average repair cost if counted. Test: only 1 in 2,000 values stays unparseable after cleanup. Zero costs (~3%) are kept as real values pending confirmation.

columns.name: sla_hours
columns.why: 999 (557 rows) and -1 (9 rows) mark unknown SLA in 7.9% of rows; left in, they inflate mean SLA targets and overstate SLA compliance. 1,046 n/a/null tokens become NULL.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Flag only for now and re-check after the multi-format parse. The share is too large to be random entry errors, so dropping rows would badly skew mean time to resolve.
options: Flag only and keep both dates
needs_human.question: 35% of comparable tickets show created_at later than resolved_at. Is this a known data entry or export problem (for example swapped columns or a timezone shift), and how should these rows be handled?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Add epoch-seconds parsing. These are probably valid timestamps, and losing them removes about 4.5% of tickets from time-to-resolve metrics.
options: Add an epoch-seconds format and parse them
needs_human.question: About 4.5% of created_at values look like 10-digit Unix epoch seconds, and the profiler has no format id for them, so they will become NULL. Should an epoch format be added to the registry?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Approve the merges. They describe the same type of request, and a full category list would also let free-text entries be mapped.
options: Merge casing only and keep synonyms separate
needs_human.question: Should 'Exterminator' and 'Pest' be merged into pest_control, and 'Plumbing Issue' into plumbing? Are there other synonym groups among the 111 distinct category values (including free-text entries like 'Elevator A-001 stuck...')?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Keep 0 as a real cost unless the business confirms it is a placeholder.
options: Keep 0 as a real zero cost
needs_human.question: About 3% of costs are exactly 0. Does 0 mean no-cost work (for example done in-house) or an unknown cost?

row_checks.why: 35.1% of comparable rows (1,866 of 5,319) show created_at after resolved_at, which would give negative times to resolve and break SLA compliance; flagging keeps them visible without dropping data until the cause (format mix or swapped columns) is confirmed.

content.text: {"domain": "support tickets", "summary": "One row per ticket. Ops managers track backlog.", "likely_metrics": ["tickets per week"], "critical_columns": ["team"], "column_tags": [{"column": "owner", "tag": "person"}, {"column": "description", "tag": "free_text"}]}

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.why: 14 rows carry 'n/a'/'null' as ticket id. A ticket with no id can't be tracked, deduplicated or joined, so these rows are rejected rather than counted twice in volume and backlog.

columns.name: created_at
columns.why: created_at comes in 8 formats. 1,863 values only make sense as month-first and none as day-first, so the 1,234 ambiguous slash dates are read as mdy. Tested: only 0.05% of rows stay unparseable. 'tbd' and '0000-00-00' become NULL so they don't skew time-to-resolution.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.why: resolved_at uses the same 8 formats as created_at. 956 values only make sense as month-first and none as day-first, so mdy is used. 48.2% of rows are empty because those tickets are still open, so the column is not required. The 16 '???' values become NULL so open-backlog and time-to-resolution figures stay correct.

columns.name: category
columns.why: 13 groups of casing and separator variants split real categories, for example 'Fire Safety' (216) and 'fire safety' (210), so ticket volume by category is undercounted. 13 placeholder values become NULL.

columns.name: priority
columns.why: 19 raw values collapse into a few levels once casing is fixed, for example critical (564) and CRITICAL (558). Without this, time-to-resolution by priority and escalation counts are split in half.

columns.name: status
columns.why: 20 placeholder statuses ('null', 'unknown', '???') become NULL so they don't show up as a fake status bucket in open-backlog reporting.

columns.name: building
columns.why: 19 placeholder buildings ('???', 'unknown') become NULL so cost per building doesn't book spend to a building that doesn't exist.

columns.name: description
columns.why: 8 descriptions are placeholders ('.', 'null') and become NULL. The free text is otherwise kept as written so ticket content isn't changed.

columns.name: submitted_by
columns.why: 3 casing-only groups split the same submitter, for example 328 and 320 rows, which double-counts requesters. Only casing and whitespace are normalized; no identities are inferred.

columns.name: assigned_to
columns.why: 30.4% of tickets (3,122) have no assignee, which most likely means they are not routed yet. They stay NULL and are not treated as errors, so they still count in backlog and staffing analysis.

columns.name: cost
columns.why: 993 costs have a '$' prefix and 984 are 'n/a', 'tbd' or 'null'. 195 use -1 or -999 to mean unknown; left in, these lower vendor spend and cost per building. Empty costs (35%) stay NULL. Zero is kept for now (see question).

columns.name: sla_hours
columns.why: 999 (557 rows) and -1 (9 rows) mean the SLA is unknown in 7.9% of rows. Left in, they inflate SLA targets and overstate the SLA compliance rate. 1,046 'n/a'/'null' values also become NULL.

dedup.why: 10,258 distinct ids for about 10,260 non-null ids means a few tickets repeat. Keeping the latest version stops resolved tickets from also being counted in the backlog.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Flag only for now. The share is too large to discard, and swapping without confirmation would invent resolution times.
options: Flag only and keep both timestamps
Null resolved_at when it is before created_at
needs_human.question: 35% of resolved tickets (1,866) appear to be resolved before they were created. Are created_at and resolved_at swapped at the source, or are these data-entry errors?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Keep 0 for now. Internal-crew jobs can plausibly cost nothing.
needs_human.question: Does a cost of 0 mean a real zero-cost job (for example, done by an internal crew) or an unknown cost?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: mdy
needs_human.question: Slash dates are read as month-first (US). 1,863 and 956 values only make sense that way and none as day-first. Is US order correct for every source system?

row_checks.why: At least one category holds description text ('Elevator A-001 stuck be…'). Swapping those values back restores the correct category so ticket volume by category is right.

1,866 of 5,319 resolved tickets (35%) appear to be resolved before they were created, which would give negative resolution times. These rows are flagged, not deleted, until a person confirms whether the timestamps are swapped.
28 rows have 7 or more of 13 cells empty. They are flagged rather than rejected so that tickets with a valid id still count in volume while their missing fields are reviewed.

addressed_issues.reason: Only 28 rows (0.3%) have 7 or more missing cells. Rows missing ticket_id are rejected by the ticket_id rule. The rest keep their real values with NULLs, because filling them in would mean inventing data.

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.why: 14 rows carry n/a/null instead of a ticket id; without an id a ticket cannot be tracked to resolution or counted reliably in ticket volume, so those rows are rejected.

columns.name: created_at
columns.why: created_at uses 8 formats; 1,863 values prove month-first and none prove day-first, so 1,234 ambiguous slash dates are read mdy. Mis-parsed starts would corrupt mean time to resolve and SLA compliance; tbd, 0000-00-00 and unparseable values (~4.5% in a test, mostly 10-digit epoch numbers) become NULL instead of fake dates.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.why: 48.2% of tickets have no resolved_at because they are still open; these stay NULL and are not treated as errors, so they do not distort mean time to resolve. 956 values prove month-first and none prove day-first, so 630 ambiguous dates are read mdy; ??? and unparseable values become NULL.

columns.name: category
columns.why: 13 variant groups split categories (e.g. 'Fire Safety' 216 vs 'fire safety' 210; Pest/pest control/Exterminator), so ticket volume and cost by category are fragmented; mapping merges them and 13 placeholder values become NULL.

columns.name: priority
columns.why: Priority is split by casing (critical 564 vs CRITICAL 558, high 575 vs High 535); lowercasing merges 5 variant groups so SLA compliance and escalation by priority are counted once. 10 placeholders become NULL.

columns.name: status
columns.why: 20 rows hold ???/null/unknown as status; keeping them as values would create fake status buckets and distort open vs resolved counts and escalation rate.

columns.name: building
columns.why: 19 rows use ???/unknown as building; nulling them prevents a fake 'unknown' building from showing up in ticket volume and cost per building.

columns.name: description
columns.why: 8 descriptions are only '.' or 'null'; nulling them keeps text analysis and request triage from treating placeholders as real issue descriptions.

columns.name: submitted_by
columns.why: 3 casing-only variant groups split the same requester (e.g. 328 vs 320 rows); normalizing casing and whitespace merges them without inferring identities, so per-requester volume is correct.

columns.name: assigned_to
columns.why: 30.4% of tickets (3,122) have no assignee, which likely means not yet assigned; these stay NULL so routing metrics are not filled in with guessed staff or vendors.

columns.name: cost
columns.why: 993 costs have a $ prefix and would be lost as text; 984 n/a/tbd/null and 195 -1/-999 placeholders would drag down total and average repair cost if counted. Test: only 1 in 2,000 values stays unparseable after cleanup. Zero costs (~3%) are kept as real values pending confirmation.

columns.name: sla_hours
columns.why: 999 (557 rows) and -1 (9 rows) mark unknown SLA in 7.9% of rows; left in, they inflate mean SLA targets and overstate SLA compliance. 1,046 n/a/null tokens become NULL.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Flag only for now and re-check after the multi-format parse. The share is too large to be random entry errors, so dropping rows would badly skew mean time to resolve.
options: Flag only and keep both dates

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Add epoch-seconds parsing. These are probably valid timestamps, and losing them removes about 4.5% of tickets from time-to-resolve metrics.
options: Add an epoch-seconds format and parse them
needs_human.question: About 4.5% of created_at values look like 10-digit Unix epoch seconds, and the profiler has no format id for them, so they will become NULL. Should an epoch format be added to the registry?

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Approve the merges. They describe the same type of request, and a full category list would also let free-text entries be mapped.

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.why: 14 rows carry 'n/a'/'null' as ticket id. A ticket with no id can't be tracked, deduplicated or joined, so these rows are rejected rather than counted twice in volume and backlog.

columns.name: created_at
columns.why: created_at comes in 8 formats. 1,863 values only make sense as month-first and none as day-first, so the 1,234 ambiguous slash dates are read as mdy. Tested: only 0.05% of rows stay unparseable. 'tbd' and '0000-00-00' become NULL so they don't skew time-to-resolution.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.why: resolved_at uses the same 8 formats as created_at. 956 values only make sense as month-first and none as day-first, so mdy is used. 48.2% of rows are empty because those tickets are still open, so the column is not required. The 16 '???' values become NULL so open-backlog and time-to-resolution figures stay correct.

columns.name: category
columns.why: 13 groups of casing and separator variants split real categories, for example 'Fire Safety' (216) and 'fire safety' (210), so ticket volume by category is undercounted. 13 placeholder values become NULL.

columns.name: priority
columns.why: 19 raw values collapse into a few levels once casing is fixed, for example critical (564) and CRITICAL (558). Without this, time-to-resolution by priority and escalation counts are split in half.

columns.name: status
columns.why: 20 placeholder statuses ('null', 'unknown', '???') become NULL so they don't show up as a fake status bucket in open-backlog reporting.

columns.name: building
columns.why: 19 placeholder buildings ('???', 'unknown') become NULL so cost per building doesn't book spend to a building that doesn't exist.

columns.name: description
columns.why: 8 descriptions are placeholders ('.', 'null') and become NULL. The free text is otherwise kept as written so ticket content isn't changed.

columns.name: submitted_by
columns.why: 3 casing-only groups split the same submitter, for example 328 and 320 rows, which double-counts requesters. Only casing and whitespace are normalized; no identities are inferred.

columns.name: assigned_to
columns.why: 30.4% of tickets (3,122) have no assignee, which most likely means they are not routed yet. They stay NULL and are not treated as errors, so they still count in backlog and staffing analysis.

columns.name: cost
columns.why: 993 costs have a '$' prefix and 984 are 'n/a', 'tbd' or 'null'. 195 use -1 or -999 to mean unknown; left in, these lower vendor spend and cost per building. Empty costs (35%) stay NULL. Zero is kept for now (see question).

columns.name: sla_hours
columns.why: 999 (557 rows) and -1 (9 rows) mean the SLA is unknown in 7.9% of rows. Left in, they inflate SLA targets and overstate the SLA compliance rate. 1,046 'n/a'/'null' values also become NULL.

dedup.why: 10,258 distinct ids for about 10,260 non-null ids means a few tickets repeat. Keeping the latest version stops resolved tickets from also being counted in the backlog.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Flag only for now. The share is too large to discard, and swapping without confirmation would invent resolution times.
options: Flag only and keep both timestamps

needs_human.agent_recommendation: Keep 0 for now. Internal-crew jobs can plausibly cost nothing.

needs_human.agent_recommendation: mdy
needs_human.question: Slash dates are read as month-first (US). 1,863 and 956 values only make sense that way and none as day-first. Is US order correct for every source system?

row_checks.why: At least one category holds description text ('Elevator A-001 stuck be…'). Swapping those values back restores the correct category so ticket volume by category is right.

1,866 of 5,319 resolved tickets (35%) appear to be resolved before they were created, which would give negative resolution times. These rows are flagged, not deleted, until a person confirms whether the timestamps are swapped.
28 rows have 7 or more of 13 cells empty. They are flagged rather than rejected so that tickets with a valid id still count in volume while their missing fields are reviewed.
